name: filing_sim
hypothesis: Firms that rewrite much of their 10-K vs last year's (low similarity) earn lower future returns: managers change disclosures when news (often bad) arrives, investors rarely compare filings side by side, so prices adjust slowly over months. For ASAM (long-only): a screen of stocks to avoid.
definition: Cosine similarity (word counts) between a firm's original 10-K and its most recent original 10-K filed 9-15 months earlier (WRDS bow_cossim, lookback 1-4, amendments skipped). Low = changer. Monthly value = latest with published_date <= month-end, at most 15 months old.
source: WRDS SEC Analytics Suite, wrdssec.bow_cossim (Bag of Words); linked via wrdssec.wciklink_gvkey and CRSP-Compustat (ccmxpf_lnkhist)
citation: Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen (2020), Lazy Prices, Journal of Finance 75(3), 1371ff., doi:10.1111/jofi.12885
inputs_required: 10-K text similarity (cosine), SEC acceptance date and time, EDGAR filing date, CIK-gvkey link, CCM link, NYSE trading days
timing_rule: exact: SEC acceptance time (New York) at or before 4 p.m. -> same trading day; after 4 p.m. or no time -> next trading day; acceptance date after the EDGAR filing date (WRDS re-processing date, mostly 1994-2002) -> EDGAR filing date, next trading day
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Usable from 1998 (EDGAR phase-in); last filings 2024-12, so 2025 values are 2024 10-Ks. Column format_change_2010_14 flags values from 10-Ks published 2010-2014: a filing-format change tripled 10-K length; in 2010-2012 the largest firms were 57-63% of the bottom fifth (English-only cosine_eng did not fix it). Paper's sample ends 2014 -> 2015-2024 is out of sample. Process and decisions: signals/lazy_prices/progress.md.

name: net_issuance
hypothesis: Firms that shrink their split-adjusted share count (net buybacks) earn higher future returns and net issuers lower: managers sell shares when they think the stock is expensive and buy back when cheap, and investors underreact. Slow (a year or more). For ASAM (long-only): tilt toward net buyers-back; one half of the issuance + insider-cluster combination.
definition: 12-month log change in split-adjusted shares outstanding (CRSP shrout x mthcumfacshr) with a 4-month skip: ln(adj[t-4]/adj[t-16]). Positive = net issuer, negative = net buyer-back. Firm level: a firm with 2+ listed share classes gets one value for all classes, ln(sum W / sum W*exp(-x_class)) with W = class market value at t (per-class value in net_issuance_class). No value unless every month of the window has a CRSP price.
source: CRSP CIZ crsp.msf_v2 (shrout, mthcumfacshr, mthprc); timing measured with CRSP share history (crsp.stkshares) and EDGAR filing dates (wrdssec.wrds_forms)
citation: Pontiff & Woodgate (2008), Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance 63(2), 921-945, doi:10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01335.x
inputs_required: CRSP monthly shares outstanding, cumulative share-adjustment factor, price; for the checks also total return, CRSP share history, EDGAR 10-K/10-Q filing dates, CIK-gvkey and CCM links
location: data/issuance_insider/net_issuance_monthly.parquet:net_issuance (checks in the same file: net_issuance_skip3, net_issuance_skip6, net_issuance_pit, comp_issuance, net_issuance_5y; events: data/issuance_insider/net_issuance_events.parquet); shared drive
timing_rule: assumed: share counts used 4 months after their month. CRSP dates many counts at the fiscal period end, before the 10-K/10-Q is public; measured 2003-2025, a 4-month skip uses under 1% of share changes before public (1 month: 34-56%). Check net_issuance_pit uses each count's 10-K/10-Q public time (at or before 4 p.m. -> same trading day, else next) where matched.
test_results: Backtest 2026-11-16 (firm level across share classes; investable: price >= $5, me >= $250M; monthly; 1980-2025): Q5 (net buyback) beat the market +2.2%/yr VW (t 2.4), +2.8% EW (t 2.0); Q5-Q1 6.3%/yr EW (t 3.4); Fama-MacBeth with reversal, bm, size 5.6%/yr (t 3.0); FF5+UMD alpha of Q5 small (VW +0.7%, t 1.3; loads on RMW, HML, CMA); weaker 2008-2025 (Q5-Q1 VW 3.1%, t 1.1); annual December check Q5 VW +1.6%/yr vs market (t 2.2). Details: signals/issuance_insider/backtest.md.
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Primary fixed before any return test; named checks in the same file: net_issuance_skip3, net_issuance_skip6, net_issuance_pit, comp_issuance (Daniel-Titman 1-year composite issuance, counts dividends), net_issuance_5y. 88.8% of panel rows have a value (new listings need 16 months). Extremes are real (serial diluters; SPAC trust redemptions look like large buybacks - consider excluding SIC 6770). One half of the issuance_insider project with insider_cluster; combinations C1 (net shrinker and insider cluster buy) and C2 (average rank) use the two primaries only. Process and decisions: signals/issuance_insider/progress.md. Changed 2026-11-16 to firm level across share classes (per-class values let conversions look like buybacks, e.g. Berkshire A -> B); ~1% of rows affected.

name: insider_cluster
hypothesis: When several officers or directors of a firm buy its stock on the open market within a day of each other, the stock earns higher returns over the following weeks to months: insiders know more about the firm, several buying together is a stronger signal than one, and investors underreact to the Form 4 filings. Purchases only (insider sales are mostly for liquidity). For ASAM (long-only): a buy-side screen; one half of the issuance + insider-cluster combination.
definition: Number of different officers/directors whose purchase (Form 4/5 code P, acquired, common stock, original filings, filed 0-90 days after the trade) was part of a tight cluster - another officer/director of the same firm (gvkey) bought on the same or an adjacent trading day - and became public, with its partner's filing, in months t-2..t. 0 = no cluster (firm's filings visible); blank = firm not linked to SEC filings, or before 2006-03. A joint filing counts as one insider; the firm-level value goes to every permno of the gvkey.
source: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (Forms 3/4/5 XML as filed, quarterly 2006Q1-2025Q4, sec.gov, free); issuer CIK -> gvkey via wrdssec.wciklink_gvkey (dated link; a CIK linking to only one gvkey is used outside its dates) -> permno via CRSP-Compustat (ccmxpf_lnkhist); NYSE trading days from CRSP
citation: Kang, Kim & Wang (2018), Cluster Trading of Corporate Insiders, working paper (UNSW / UW-Milwaukee / UCF); see also Alldredge & Blank (2019), Do Insiders Cluster Trades with Colleagues? Evidence from Daily Insider Trading, Journal of Financial Research 42(2), 331-360, doi:10.1111/jfir.12172
inputs_required: Form 3/4/5 non-derivative transactions (code, acquired/disposed, trade date, shares, price, security title), filing date, form type, reporting owner and relationship, issuer CIK; CIK-gvkey link, CCM link, NYSE trading days; panel market value (check insider_buy_value_3m)
location: data/issuance_insider/insider_cluster_monthly.parquet:insider_cluster (checks in the same file: insider_buyers_1m, insider_buy_value_3m, insider_npr_6m; events: data/issuance_insider/insider_cluster_events.parquet; raw SEC pull: data/issuance_insider/sec_trans/sec_submissions/sec_owners.parquet); shared drive
timing_rule: exact: Form 4/5 filing date -> next trading day (the SEC data sets have no time of day; assumed after the close); a cluster purchase counts once its earliest partner's filing is also public; trades filed more than 90 days after the trade dropped
test_results: Backtest 2026-11-16 (investable; monthly; 2006-04 to 2025-12): no premium. Cluster portfolio vs market -2.9%/yr EW (t -1.3), -3.9% VW (t -1.6); FF5+UMD alpha -0.8% EW (t -0.5), -2.5% VW (t -1.1); Fama-MacBeth with controls -1.4%/yr (t -0.6); named checks not significant; C1 underperforms, C2 = net_issuance alone. Small caps not tested. Details: signals/issuance_insider/backtest.md.
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs). Primary fixed before any return test; named checks in the same file: insider_buyers_1m (buyers made public in month t), insider_buy_value_3m (purchase dollars over 3 months / firm market value - keeps price typos up to 377,051x, use by rank only), insider_npr_6m (net purchase ratio over 6 months, insider-days). 96.9% of panel rows from 2006-06 have a value; 6.8% have a cluster (46% of purchase insider-days are clustered; Kang et al.: over 40%). Kept on purpose ('keep everything'): every code P counts, incl. IPO and offering purchases (7 of the 10 largest clusters in the stock's IPO month; 4.8% of cluster months in a stock's first 3 CRSP months) and plan-like fractional purchases; a CRSP daily price check would be a new, separately recorded version. No data before 2006 (LSEG insider data not readable on the WRDS account; library asked). Anchor sample 1986-2016, so 2017-2025 is out of sample. Combinations C1/C2 with net_issuance use the primaries only. Process and decisions: signals/issuance_insider/progress.md.

name: rd_to_market
hypothesis: Firms that spend a lot on R&D relative to their market value earn higher future returns: U.S. accounting expenses R&D at once, so heavy researchers report low earnings and book value even when the research builds valuable intangible capital; investors anchored on reported numbers under-price them, above all beaten-down ones. A risk story predicts the same sign. Slow (months to years). For ASAM (long-only): a tilt toward high R&D-to-market among firms that do R&D.
definition: rdm = R&D expense (Compustat xrd) from the latest annual 10-K public by the month-end / the firm's market value at the month-end (sum of its share classes in the panel, by CRSP permco); = 1000 x xrd ($ millions) / me ($ thousands). R&D firms only: xrd = 0 or missing -> has_rd = 0, rdm blank. Signal on the CCM-linked (primary) share class; other classes blank. An R&D figure is usable until 18 months after its fiscal year-end. Non-USD R&D blank (247 panel rows). Check column rdm_hxz: Hou-Xue-Zhang Rdm (xrd for the fiscal year ending in calendar y-1 / firm market value at December y-1, held July y to June y+1).
source: Compustat comp.funda (xrd; INDL/STD/D/C) with 10-K filing dates from comp.co_filedate; market value from the panel (CRSP), share classes by CRSP permco (crsp.msf_v2); CRSP-Compustat link (ccmxpf_lnkhist); NYSE trading days from CRSP
citation: Chan, Lakonishok & Sougiannis (2001), The Stock Market Valuation of Research and Development Expenditures, Journal of Finance 56(6), 2431-2456, doi:10.1111/0022-1082.00411; see also Hou, Xue & Zhang (2020), Replicating Anomalies, Review of Financial Studies 33(5), 2019-2133, doi:10.1093/rfs/hhy131 (Rdm); Chen & Zimmermann, Open Source Asset Pricing (RD)
inputs_required: annual R&D expense (xrd), fiscal year-end, reporting currency; 10-K filing date and time; month-end market value of every listed share class; permco; CCM link; NYSE trading days
location: data/rd_to_market/rd_to_market_monthly.parquet:rdm (same file: has_rd, status, rdm_hxz; events: data/rd_to_market/rd_events.parquet); shared drive
frequency: monthly (R&D updates at each 10-K; market value every month)
timing_rule: exact: 10-K filing date (comp.co_filedate); its time of day is stored in UTC, converted to New York: before 4 p.m. -> same trading day, otherwise or no time -> next trading day; no 10-K date -> datadate + 6 months as month-end (assumed: 8.6% of signal rows; 23% in 1980-84, <= 4% from 2000); very late filing dates trusted; values restated (Compustat current)
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). Signal on 37.9% of panel rows (30% in 1980 to 50% in 2025); 56.3% of rows are firms reporting no R&D. Validated 2026-11-22: 0 look-ahead; 3 firms match their 10-Ks; Open Source Asset Pricing RD rank correlation 0.99 (identical for the same fiscal year; we switch at the 10-K date, OSAP after 6 months). Extremes are tiny or distressed firms (max 457x) - use ranks or winsorize; one-off acquired in-process R&D inflates some years (33 firm-years where R&D tripled above $1bn, e.g. Merck 2023) - test with and without. Firm market value counts only listed share classes (e.g. Alphabet Class B left out), as in OSAP. Paper's sample 1975-1995, published 2001, so 2002-2025 is out of sample. Process and decisions: signals/rd_to_market/progress.md.

name: prisk
hypothesis: Firms whose earnings calls discuss political risk more face undiversifiable policy risk and should earn higher returns (pre-registered). Not supported 2003-2021 in large caps.
definition: prisk4 = mean of the last 4 quarterly PRisk scores (>=3) published by the month-end; PRisk = political bigrams near risk words / transcript bigrams. Variants in the same file: prisk (last call), prisk_dm / prisk_dm4 (minus own previous-8-call mean), nprisk4, risk4, psent4, 8 topic scores.
source: firmlevelrisk.com firmquarter_2021q1.csv (free); gvkey -> panel gvkey -> permno
citation: Hassan, Hollander, van Lent & Tahoun (2019), Firm-Level Political Risk: Measurement and Effects, QJE 134(4), 2135-2202, doi:10.1093/qje/qjz021
inputs_required: earnings-call date and PRisk per firm-quarter; panel gvkey
timing_rule: exact: call date -> next business day (call hour unknown); value unused if the call is older than 6 months
test_results: 2026-11-24, annual Dec formation, NYSE-median universe: design 2003-2012 Q5-Q1 -3.4%/yr (t -1.4), alpha -2.4 (t NW -5.3 / OLS -1.5), p.258 screen FAIL; holdout 2013-2021 +0.7%/yr (t 0.5); FM with controls design -0.9 (t -0.5), holdout +1.6 (t 2.0); 10 variants, DSR 0.00. Only prisk_dm4 positive in both halves (+1.2%/yr, full t 2.3). Details: signals/prisk/test_results.md.
notes: Stocks only. Ranks only (14% zeros, max 11,057). Every permno of a gvkey gets the value. 2022-2025 vintages not pulled. Process: signals/prisk/progress.md.

name: earn_stability
hypothesis: Firms with stable earnings (low variation of ROA) earn higher returns (quality / low-risk). Lower = better.
definition: roa_sd5 = std (ddof=1) of panel roa at months t, t-3, ..., t-57 (20 quarterly samples), >= 12 non-missing. Check: gprof_sd5, same on gprof.
source: crsp_monthly_ratios_clean.parquet (roa, gprof)
timing_rule: assumed: panel ratios public by month-end (as the panel)
test_results: 2026-11-24, lab default: design 1986-2005 low-minus-high +2.7%/yr (t 0.8), alpha -4.1 (t -1.1); holdout 2006-2025 -1.9%/yr (t -0.9); screen pass both; VW alpha -6.8%/yr (t -3.1); FM with vol36: design +3.5 (t 1.2), holdout -2.1 (t -1.0); DSR 0.37 (4 trials). Adds nothing beyond vol36 (Spearman 0.65). Details: signals/earn_stability/test_results.md.
notes: roa is trailing-12-month, so quarterly samples overlap. Process: signals/earn_stability/progress.md.

name: net_operating_assets
hypothesis: Firms with bloated balance sheets - high net operating assets relative to last year's total assets - earn lower future returns. NOA is the running total of reported operating income minus free cash flow, so a high NOA means past earnings have not turned into cash; investors with limited attention focus on earnings and over-value these firms, and prices correct as profits fail to keep up. Bloat builds up through accruals (earnings quality), over-investment, and the equity or debt that pays for both. Slow (one to three years). For ASAM (long-only): a tilt away from high-NOA firms.
definition: noa = (operating assets - operating liabilities) / total assets of the previous fiscal year, from the latest annual 10-K public by the month-end (Hirshleifer-Hou-Teoh-Zhang 2004, as published): operating assets = at - che; operating liabilities = at - dlc - dltt - mib - pstk - ceq; i.e. (ceq + pstk + mib + dltt + dlc - che) / at_prev. Missing che, dlc, dltt, mib, pstk = 0; at > 0 and ceq required; previous fiscal year-end 10-14 months earlier with at > 0. Every firm gets a value (financial flag for SIC 6000-6999). Signal on the CCM-linked (primary) share class; other classes blank. Usable until 18 months after fiscal year-end. Side columns: noa_mi (robustness only: operating liabilities = lt - dlc - dltt, which treats nonredeemable minority interest as financing from fiscal 2009 on; identical before 2009), noa_at_cur (same numerator / this year's at), dnoa (change in NOA / at_prev), asset_growth (at / at_prev - 1). Parts of NOA (receivables, inventory, PP&E, intangibles, goodwill, other operating assets, operating liabilities, payables, equity, debt, cash; all / at_prev) in the event file.
source: Compustat comp.funda (at, che, dlc, dltt, mib, pstk, ceq, lt, rect, invt, ppent, intan, gdwl, ap; mibn, mibt for checks; INDL/STD/D/C) with 10-K filing dates from comp.co_filedate; CRSP-Compustat link (ccmxpf_lnkhist); share classes by CRSP permco (crsp.msf_v2); industry (financial flag) from the panel's CRSP siccd; NYSE trading days from CRSP
citation: Hirshleifer, Hou, Teoh & Zhang (2004), Do Investors Overvalue Firms with Bloated Balance Sheets?, Journal of Accounting and Economics 38(1), 297-331; see also Hou, Xue & Zhang (2020), Replicating Anomalies, Review of Financial Studies 33(5), 2019-2133, doi:10.1093/rfs/hhy131 (Noa, dNoa); Chen & Zimmermann, Open Source Asset Pricing (NOA, dNoa)
inputs_required: annual total assets, cash and short-term investments, debt in current liabilities, long-term debt, minority interest, preferred stock, common equity, total liabilities (and receivables, inventory, PP&E, intangibles, goodwill, payables for the parts); fiscal year-end; 10-K filing date and time; previous fiscal year's total assets; CCM link; permco; CRSP SIC code; NYSE trading days
location: data/net_operating_assets/noa_monthly.parquet:noa (same file: noa_mi, noa_at_cur, dnoa, asset_growth, financial, status; events with the parts of NOA: data/net_operating_assets/noa_events.parquet); shared drive
timing_rule: exact: 10-K filing date (comp.co_filedate); its time of day is stored in UTC, converted to New York: before 4 p.m. -> same trading day, otherwise or no time -> next trading day; no 10-K date -> datadate + 6 months as month-end (assumed: 9.1% of signal rows; 30% in 1980-84, <= 3% from 2000); very late filing dates trusted; values restated (Compustat current)
notes: Stocks only (panel has no ETFs; ETF rows would be n/a). noa on 88.0% of panel rows (75% in the mid-1980s, >= 95% from 2005); financial firms 16-22% of rows. Validated 2026-11-23: 0 look-ahead; Microsoft, Walmart, Boeing match their 10-Ks; splits do not move it; dNoa identical to Open Source Asset Pricing in 99.9% of same-fiscal-year rows. Known differences and limitations: (1) OSAP's NOA leaves short-term debt (dlc) out of the numerator; ours follows the paper (Compustat item 34) and Hou-Xue-Zhang, so NOA rank correlation with OSAP is 0.88. (2) ASC 842: from fiscal 2019 Compustat puts operating-lease liabilities in dlc/dltt, raising NOA for lease-heavy firms (median retail & restaurants 0.56 -> 0.86 in the adoption year, then about +0.1); not fixed - lease items are only in Compustat Snapshot, which this subscription can't read; flag or drop the adoption year for lease-heavy industries in tests. (3) Extremes (|noa| > 5 on 0.47% of rows) are SPACs/shells with ~$0 prior-year assets or huge one-year growth - use ranks or winsorize. (4) 4.1% of signal rows have negative equity. (5) Restated Compustat values. Primary signal fixed before any test: noa; noa_mi is a robustness check only. Paper's sample 1964-2002, published Dec 2004, so 2005-2025 is out of sample. Process and decisions: signals/net_operating_assets/progress.md.
